items.headline: RTS Link could shift over S$1 billion of Singapore spending to Johor Bahru
items.summary: A joint study by three Singapore business bodies projects Singaporeans will spend an extra S$1.05 billion a year in Johor Bahru once the RTS Link opens in 2027, against S$756 million flowing in, a net S$290 million outflow, with cross-border trips up 51%.

items.headline: Lawyer-politician Lim Tean ordered to surrender on 20 July to begin jail term
items.summary: The Court of Appeal ordered People's Alliance for Reform figure Lim Tean, 61, to surrender on 20 July to serve three months and one week in jail for practising law on 32 occasions in 2021 without a valid certificate.

items.headline: Over-height lorry driver jailed 13 months for S$1.45 million CTE tunnel damage
items.summary: Lai Daohong, 56, was jailed 13 months and banned from driving for two years after an over-height lorry struck the Central Expressway tunnel ceiling at Cairnhill Circle in 2024, closing the road for 10 hours and causing about S$1.45 million in damage.

items.headline: Man, 23, jailed four months over 181km/h CTE midnight joyride crash
items.summary: Lee Jun En Gilviz, 23, was jailed four months and banned for three years for dangerous driving after a six-car midnight joyride in 2024 ended in a crash, having driven at up to 181km/h on the Central Expressway.

items.headline: Skyroot to attempt India's first private orbital launch, Vikram-1, on 18 July
items.summary: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace plans to launch Vikram-1, India's first privately developed orbital rocket, from Sriharikota on 18 July in a mission called Aagaman, carrying technology-demonstration payloads.

items.headline: Re-NEET-UG 2026 results declared; two candidates share the top rank at 715
items.summary: The NTA declared the re-conducted NEET-UG 2026 results on 16 July, with Punjab's Aryan Gupta and Haryana's Panshul Bansal sharing AIR 1 at 715 out of 720. About 11.21 lakh qualified in the 21 June retest held after a paper leak.

items.headline: Supreme Court says a third language should begin in Class 6, not Class 9
items.summary: Hearing a challenge to CBSE's three-language policy, the Supreme Court said a compulsory third language from Class 9 would cause avoidable exam stress and should start around Class 6, declined an interim stay, and listed the matter for 22 July.

items.headline: ED raids 13 locations in a Rohingya-Bangladeshi infiltration and terror-funding probe
items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate searched 13 premises across Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana and West Bengal under the money-laundering law on 16 July, targeting an alleged syndicate smuggling Rohingya and Bangladeshi nationals into India, from a 2024 UP ATS FIR.

items.headline: Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj loses leaders to the BJP before the Bankipur bypoll
items.summary: Several Jan Suraaj leaders, including mathematician K.C. Sinha and former 2025 candidates Bittu Singh and Gopal Singh, joined the BJP in Bihar ahead of the 30 July Bankipur bypoll, where Prashant Kishor contests against the BJP's Neeraj Kumar Sinha.

items.headline: Burnham set to name Shabana Mahmood as chancellor, passing over Miliband
items.summary: Incoming prime minister Andy Burnham is expected to make Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood his chancellor, per FT reporting, passing over Ed Miliband, Yvette Cooper and Wes Streeting, with cabinet appointments due Monday 20 July.

items.headline: IMF warns Burnham against raising the top income-tax rate as it nudges up growth
items.summary: In its 2026 Article IV assessment, the IMF cautioned Andy Burnham that raising the top income-tax rate would hurt growth and said Britain is near 'peak tax', while lifting its 2026 UK growth forecast to about 1.0%.

items.headline: UK economy grew 0.1% in May as services offset falls in industry
items.summary: ONS data showed GDP rose 0.1% in May, reversing April's fall, driven by 0.3% services growth while production dropped 0.5% and construction 0.8%; output was up 0.7% over three months, though the FTSE 100 and gilts slipped.

items.headline: UK proposes an overnight social-media curfew for 16- and 17-year-olds
items.summary: The government announced a default lockout from midnight to 6am for 16- and 17-year-olds on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, with autoplay and infinite scrolling off by default and an opt-out, expected by spring 2027, after an under-16 ban announced last month.

items.headline: Update: US launches a sixth night of strikes on Iran and disables a tanker as Tehran hits the Gulf
items.summary: US Central Command struck sites near Qeshm Island, Bandar Abbas and Chabahar and disabled an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, in a sixth consecutive night leaving at least 35 dead and 300+ wounded; Tehran said it hit US assets in Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan.

items.headline: French parliament approves a landmark assisted-dying bill
items.summary: France's parliament gave final approval to a bill legalising assisted dying for adults with incurable, life-threatening illnesses, one of the most significant social reforms of President Macron's second term.

items.headline: Hundreds protest in Kyiv over Zelenskyy's dismissal of his defence minister
items.summary: Hundreds gathered in central Kyiv to protest President Zelenskyy's abrupt sacking of the defence minister, one of the largest wartime demonstrations against the government, demanding transparency over the reshuffle.

items.headline: US to impose 25% tariffs on a range of Brazilian imports under Section 301
items.summary: The White House said it will levy 25% duties on thousands of Brazilian goods including sugar, apparel, paper and steel, the first tariffs under a new strategy using Section 301 of US trade law.

items.headline: Update: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 2,000 cases as health workers strike
items.summary: The DR Congo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 2,000 recorded cases, the WHO and authorities said, as more health workers began strike action over pay and conditions, threatening the response across several eastern provinces.

items.headline: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines releases its first open model, Inkling
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling, a mixture-of-experts model with 975 billion total parameters (about 41 billion active) trained on 45 trillion multimodal tokens, under Apache 2.0 with open weights.

items.headline: Apple Intelligence cleared for China launch via Alibaba's Qwen model
items.summary: Apple secured Chinese regulatory approval to bring Apple Intelligence to the mainland by integrating Alibaba's Qwen model across iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS, clearing a long-standing block on its generative-AI features.

items.headline: Toyota-backed Walden Robotics exits stealth at a $1.1 billion valuation
items.summary: Humanoid-robot startup Walden Robotics, spun out of a Toyota lab, emerged from stealth with about $300 million seed funding at a $1.1 billion valuation, backed by Toyota, Nvidia, Boeing and Samsung Ventures, and is piloting a robot at a Toyota factory.

items.headline: Google's AI Mode can now link to and act inside third-party apps
items.summary: Google began rolling out 'Connected Apps' in AI Mode for US users on 16 July, letting people act within search, adding items to an Instacart cart, generating Canva templates, or building a YouTube Music playlist.

items.headline: Roblox launches an AI 'Build' feature to make games from text prompts
items.summary: Roblox added a mobile feature called Build that turns plain-text prompts into playable games with no coding; a public alpha begins 28 July, initially for users aged nine and up in New Zealand.

items.headline: Netflix falls 8% despite Q2 revenue rising 13% to $12.56 billion
items.summary: Netflix reported Q2 revenue of $12.56 billion, up 13%, and EPS of 80 cents, narrowly beating on profit while just missing revenue; shares fell over 8% after hours on a narrowed full-year revenue outlook of $51.0-$51.4 billion.

items.headline: Bank of America profit jumps 27% as trading and dealmaking rebound
items.summary: Bank of America posted Q2 net income of $9.1 billion, up 27%, on revenue up 15% to $31.6 billion; equities-trading revenue surged about 70% to $3.6 billion, extending Wall Street's trading boom into a 17th straight quarter of growth.

items.headline: GE Aerospace lifts its full-year profit outlook as engine demand stays strong
items.summary: GE Aerospace raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $7.65-$7.85 after Q2 adjusted revenue rose 24% to $12.6 billion and adjusted EPS climbed 22% to $2.02, citing strong services growth and 31% higher engine deliveries.

items.headline: UnitedHealth raises its 2026 profit outlook as Q2 revenue hits $112 billion
items.summary: UnitedHealth reported Q2 revenue of $112.0 billion and adjusted EPS of $6.38, and lifted full-year adjusted guidance to $19.50-$20.00, crediting improved margins after exiting unprofitable contracts and a $1.5 billion AI investment.

items.headline: Wall Street slips as a chip selloff overshadows strong earnings
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.51% to 7,533.77 and the Nasdaq dropped 1.47% to 25,881.95 as chip stocks slid, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF down nearly 4% after TSMC's raised capital-spending forecast; Arm fell more than 5%.

items.headline: England level the ODI series as Root falls one short of a hundred in Cardiff
items.summary: Joe Root's unbeaten 99 off 133 balls steered England past India's 233 to a four-wicket win in the second ODI at Cardiff, levelling the series 1-1; the decider is at Lord's on 19 July.

items.headline: F1 heads to Spa as the Belgian Grand Prix weekend gets under way
items.summary: The 2026 Belgian Grand Prix runs 17-19 July at Spa-Francorchamps, with the 44-lap race on Sunday; leader Kimi Antonelli arrives 25 points clear of George Russell after Charles Leclerc's British GP win, with rain forecast.

items.headline: Verstappen stonewalls future questions at Spa: There's nothing to say
items.summary: In the Spa press conference, Max Verstappen again refused to address McLaren speculation or commit to Red Bull for 2027, saying there's nothing to say while calling the team like a second family; he sits seventh on 76 points.

items.headline: Sakkari delights the home crowd, routing Dart to reach the Athens quarters
items.summary: Maria Sakkari dropped just three games in a 6-1, 6-2 win over Britain's Harriet Dart to reach the Athens Open quarterfinals on home soil; she next faces Alycia Parks.

items.headline: Zheng Qinwen reaches her first quarterfinal in 13 months at Athens
items.summary: Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen beat qualifier Elena Micic 6-4, 6-1 in Athens to reach her first WTA quarterfinal since June 2025, continuing her return from injury.

items.headline: A Maya wall formula reveals the first named ancient mathematician, Sak Tahn Waax
items.summary: Researchers deciphering microtexts on a wall at Xultun in Guatemala found astronomical calculations signed 'so says Sak Tahn Waax', dated 781 CE, the only known Classic-period Maya mathematician-astronomer named and claiming credit, published in Antiquity.

items.headline: Mathematicians close in on the hidden order inside chaos
items.summary: A new result in Ramsey theory comes astonishingly close to an upper bound largely unchanged since the 1930s; emeritus NYU mathematician Joel Spencer, a frequent Erdos collaborator, called it a tremendous breakthrough.

items.headline: A remarkable new monkey species with orange lips and a froglike roar is described in Congo
items.summary: Scientists formally described Colobus congoensis, locally Likweli, from Congo's Lomami National Park, confirmed by genetic analysis in PLOS One, the fifth new African monkey species named in 75 years; an Endangered listing is proposed.

items.headline: Stem cells are coaxed into early human sperm inside a lab-grown mini-testis
items.summary: Researchers turned human stem cells into germ-cell-like cells that self-organised with mouse fetal testis tissue into tubule-like structures, producing spermatogonia six months after transplant, though cells stalled before maturity, offering a window on male infertility.

items.headline: TESS finds a planet 40,000 light-years away using an Einstein prediction
items.summary: Astronomers found a super-Jupiter, Gaia23bra b, hidden in archived NASA TESS data about 40,000 light-years away, over 250 times TESS's usual range, spotted via gravitational microlensing after a 2023 Gaia flash flagged the same patch of sky.

fun_fact.headline: Carrots were originally purple, not orange
fun_fact.body: Carrots were not always orange. For centuries the cultivated carrot was mostly purple, white, and yellow, tracing back to Persia around a thousand years ago. The familiar orange root rose to dominance only in the 16th and 17th centuries, when Dutch growers crossbred yellow and other strains into a sweeter, hardier variety.
fun_fact.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica; horticultural histories (The Conversation, World Carrot Museum)

puzzle.title: Bridge in the Dark
puzzle.body: Four travellers must cross a rickety bridge at night with one torch; the bridge holds at most two at a time and the torch must be walked back. They cross in 1, 2, 5, and 10 minutes, and a pair moves at the slower pace. What is the least total time for all four to cross?
puzzle.approach: Check whether sending the two slowest across together, using the two fastest as torch-bearers, beats always returning the fastest.
puzzle.answer: 17 minutes: 1&2 cross (2), 1 returns (1), 5&10 cross (10), 2 returns (2), 1&2 cross (2) = 17.

word_puzzle.title: The Missing Half
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into 4 groups of 4; in each group every word can be followed by the same hidden word. BUTTER, DRAGON, HORSE, MAY / SUN, WALL, CORN, WILD / FIRE, LIGHT, GREEN, WARE / WATER, RAIN, WIND, FREE.
word_puzzle.approach: Each word is half of a compound; find the shared second word for each group of four, minding overlap traps.
word_puzzle.answer: Endings FLY (BUTTER, DRAGON, HORSE, MAY), FLOWER (SUN, WALL, CORN, WILD), HOUSE (FIRE, LIGHT, GREEN, WARE), FALL (WATER, RAIN, WIND, FREE).
